solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American brings up timeless, revolutionary writer

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
time is abbreviated T, so being without time means that letter is dropped

parts.note: to bring up food is to be sick

explanation.surface: A US citizen throws up on reading a radical author who ignores time.
explanation.walkthrough: VOMITS loses its T, then the remainder turns round behind A to give ASIMOV.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction author, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: More appalling clothing article? I can't make my mind up!

definitions.text: I can't make my mind up!
definitions.note: the exclamation is what the answer would say, standing for the person

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: dire means dreadful, so more appalling is direr
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over a hideous garment, unable to decide whether to wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is not a description but the very words the indecisive person would say, standing in for that person.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditherer is an indecisive person, the kind who keeps saying they cannot decide.

clue.text: Skill of government ministers, say, about getting good deal

parts.note: to state is to say
C is short for circa, about
a raft of things is a good deal of them

explanation.surface: A report on how cabinet members, talking about it, landed a favourable agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs all the way to 'ministers'; 'say' starts the wordplay, not 'ministers, say' as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of running a country, the skill expected of those in government.

clue.text: Asian city put up gargantuan houses

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards
the word houses the answer, holding it within its letters

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A city in Asia has erected enormous homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside gARGAntuan is ARGA, which read upwards is AGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: One with a high-flying job reads novel and feels agitation about it

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement
about means surrounding, so the agitation word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to stew is to fret or be agitated
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with an important career reads a novel and gets upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the rearranged letters, which STEWS wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess is a flight attendant, whose work is literally carried out high in the air.

clue.text: Record company gives away pounds for one in Genesis

indicators.note: something given away is no longer held, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a record label is a music company
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A music company donates money to fund a performer in the band Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' looks like the rock band but means the first book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel, son of Adam and Eve killed by Cain, is a character in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Crashed car with Ned Kelly, say

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked, so its letters end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car crash involving the Australian outlaw Ned Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger, but the surname points to Gene Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Kelly was a celebrated film hoofer, so he is an example of a dancer.

clue.text: Decisive event in reporter's Asian holiday

indicators.note: a reporter delivers news by speaking, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: someone from Thailand
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Something crucial happens during a journalist's trip to Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak is the extra game or question that settles a level contest, hence a decider.

clue.text: Clingy group of relatives mean to follow son

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
one's kin are one's family
tight means stingy

explanation.surface: A needy, stingy family trails after a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothes cling closely to the body, fitting like a second skin.

clue.text: British visitor to Mecca's fare from Asia

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a haji has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A Briton travelling to Mecca eats Asian food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhaji is a spiced fried vegetable fritter from Indian cooking, a common takeaway dish.

clue.text: After second-half loss, Matt Busby maybe starts to mistrust almost revered figure

indicators.note: losing the second half means only the front part of the word survives
maybe flags an example, so the name stands for a kind of thing rather than a person

parts.note: the first half of this name
a busby is a tall fur hat worn by some soldiers

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so only the first of each word counts

parts.note: first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Manchester United's Matt Busby, after a poor second half, begins to doubt a near-saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Matt Busby was a famous Manchester United football manager, but here his names are split: a busby is a bearskin-style military hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning great soul, is an honorific for a venerated sage, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Run back with weapon, not large — pack little one?

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a liquid runs or flows

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for large is taken out

parts.note: a club is a cudgel
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Retreat with a small weapon in your pack?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack' looks like a bag to carry things in, but means a wolf pack and also a Cub Scout pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf cub is a young wolf in a pack, and in Britain the old name for a junior Scout.

clue.text: Help for official in left-leaning party, mostly

indicators.note: leaning to the left in an across clue means running right to left
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a rave is a dance party

explanation.surface: Assistance for an officer of a socialist political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-leaning party' reads as a socialist group; it means a party turned leftwards. VAR is the video assistant referee in football.
explanation.definitionFit: VAR is the video replay system that assists a football referee in reviewing decisions.

clue.text: Group of drinkers keeping a wine around that is creating positive vibe between people

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British beer-drinkers' organisation
taken as written

indicators.note: turned around means facing the opposite way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: red wine
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: Beer drinkers sharing a bottle of wine generate warm feelings among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Campaign for Real Ale is a British pressure group of beer drinkers, known by its acronym.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is friendly mutual trust and good fellowship within a group.

clue.text: Perhaps like an untested vehicle, keeping one running still

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test, so an untested car is without one
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine running is on

explanation.surface: An untested car is still kept running somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety test required for British cars over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless means not moving at all, which is the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Drops wrapping one gets out for biscuits

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
wrapping goes round something, so one word encloses the rest

parts.note: a dive is a sudden drop
I is the Roman numeral for one
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dunks a biscuit and it falls apart in the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVES opens after its D to take I and the rearranged GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Digestives are plain semi-sweet wholemeal British biscuits, often dunked in tea.

clue.text: Unknown soldiers wash anorak worn by king in film

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone is wrapped round them, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to bathe is to wash
an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast
R for rex, king

explanation.surface: Anonymous troops launder a monarch's waterproof jacket in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: An anorak is a hooded jacket, but in Britain also a nerdy obsessive; the jacket image of 'worn' hides that the coat wears the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorba the Greek is the 1964 film starring Anthony Quinn, based on Kazantzakis's novel.

clue.text: Axes guards working at role, showing excess of enthusiasm

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over, so the letters are reshaped
guards means surrounds protectively, so one set encloses the other

parts.note: z and y are axes of a graph
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Executioners keep guard while acting a part, showing too much zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools but means the y and z axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealotry is fanatical devotion, enthusiasm carried beyond reason.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
Graphic sex not initially allowed, hugging gently

indicators.note: hugging wraps around something, so one piece holds another
not initially means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: the word with its first letter dropped
p is piano, the musical marking for soft or gentle
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: Sex scenes that were not at first permitted are now shown tenderly.
explanation.walkthrough: EX and LICIT together hug P to make EXPLICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic and explicit both describe content shown in vivid, unsparing detail.

clue.text: Outcomes of great shots — a cricketer runs during defeats

indicators.note: during means within, so the pieces go inside another word

parts.note: losses are defeats
taken as written
a bat is a batsman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman scores runs while his team loses, though the shots were great.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides golf: an albatross is three under par on one hole.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an albatross is a score three strokes under par, the reward for exceptional shots.

clue.text: House of note in America, and in France

parts.note: Americans call a banknote a bill
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A home known for its music in both the USA and France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a verb here: to billet soldiers is to lodge them.
explanation.definitionFit: To billet is to provide lodging, especially for troops, so it means to house.

clue.text: Just beat the hero of a Victorian novel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to win by a tiny margin, as in at the post

definitions.text: the hero of a Victorian novel
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the narrator of a Dickens novel

explanation.walkthrough: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: To pip is to narrowly defeat, and Pip is Dickens's orphan protagonist in Great Expectations.

clue.text: Part of book, entertaining books in French course?

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a page is part of a book
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A section of a book discussing books on a French language course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick French soup, served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Source of crude attention- seeker's remark and surprised comment on line

parts.note: oi! is a call to get someone's attention
L is the abbreviation for line
well! expresses surprise

explanation.surface: The origin of vulgar remarks from a show-off, with surprised reactions online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' looks like coarse language, but it is crude oil. 'on' places WELL after L.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a borehole from which crude petroleum is extracted.

clue.text: Anthea's yummy sandwiches resembling a picnic?

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between, so the answer is held between these words

parts.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: Anthea's tasty sandwiches are perfect for a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The picnic scene points to food; 'no picnic' means difficult, so a picnic is something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is idiomatically an easy task, so being like one means being simple.

clue.text: Fan of the best vermouth in on-line catalogue?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an e-list is an electronic list
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the finest vermouth looks it up in an internet catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a classic cocktail, It being Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours rule or privilege for a select superior group.

clue.text: Singer and friend of Louis Quatorze ultimately wholly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: wholly means all

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A singer close to King Louis XIV gets completely upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis Quatorze' looks like the French king, but the definition stops at Louis: Louis Armstrong, who recorded with Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald was a jazz vocalist and a frequent recording partner of Louis Armstrong.

clue.text: They may be beside river in English city, after changing direction

indicators.note: changing direction swaps one compass-free direction letter, left, for the other, right

parts.note: a city in Yorkshire
L for left becomes R for right

explanation.surface: Places by a river in an English city that has changed course.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds swaps its L (left) for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses that grow along riverbanks.

clue.text: Joining and being in the army, I will get overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is missed out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: soldiering is serving as a soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enlisting in the army feels they will be ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joining' with the army suggests enlisting; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldering joins metal parts by melting a fusible alloy between them.
